transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (CISO, Zenith), Ethan Miles (SRE), Rajesh Patel (Head of Cloud), Nadia Thomas (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick security-focused review of Redwood's audit logs and admin activity capabilities, what fields are captured, export options (S3/Cloud Storage, SIEM integrations), retention controls, encryption/KMS, and how events map to compliance requirements (SOC 2/ISO). Customer asked about immutable retention, legal hold, and real-time alerting into their SIEM.

Topics:
- What audit events are captured (admin user changes, API keys, role changes, login, token usage, model pinning, deployment rollouts)
- Export & integration options (S3, GCS, Pub/Sub, Syslog, Splunk/Datadog connectors)
- Retention windows, tiers, and legal hold/immutable requirements
- Encryption at rest and in transit, KMS key management, customer-managed keys in VPC/private deploys
- RBAC/SSO traceability and linking to identity provider assertions

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time today. uh the plan is to run through our audit logs and admin activity, show what we capture and how you can export it. sound good?
[00:07] Priya Kumar: yep that works, quick context, we need to map artifacts for SOC 2 and ensure retention and immutability for certain events, and also we want to pipe alerts into our SIEM.
[00:14] Luis Ortega: great, i'll start with the event taxonomy, then show examples. note: transcription may have typos of product names, sorry in advance.
[00:22] Luis Ortega: so primary categories we log: auth/login events, sso assertions, api key creation/deletion, role and permission changes, admin console actions (user invite, remove), model operations like pinning a model or rolling back a version, deployment rollouts, and system generated alerts like failed deployments and quota thresholds.
[00:40] Ethan Miles: do you capture the full request payload for model calls or just admin side events? we don't want PII in logs.
[00:47] Maya Chen: good question, we do not log user prompt/request content in audit logs by default. the audit logs focus on control plane/admin actions. request/response logging is separate and controlled with customer consent and can be configured with redwood's data governance features.
[01:05] Rajesh Patel: and for admin actions, do you record who did what with an identity tieback? like the OIDC subject or SAML nameid?
[01:12] Luis Ortega: yes, for SSO flows we capture the identity assertion attributes we get from the IdP: subject/id, email, groups when available, and we include session id, source ip, agent string, and a request id that ties to other observability traces. occasionally group names are truncated in the transcript export for length, but the raw JSON has the full claim set.
[01:35] Priya Kumar: can you show an example event?
[01:38] Luis Ortega: sure, i'll paste a sanitized sample—
[01:42] [screen share briefly discussed]
[01:50] Luis Ortega: example: event_type: admin.user.update, actor: priya.kumar@zenith.com, timestamp, ip: 34.12.5.10, action: changed role -> admin, object: user_id: u-12345, before: role: analyst, after: role: admin, request_id: r-9f8e.
[02:12] Nadia Thomas: that level looks good. what about API key usage? we need to see creation and revocation and token rotation events.
[02:18] Luis Ortega: yes we log api_key.create and api_key.revoke and api_key.rotate, we don't store token plaintext. metadata includes key id, owner, creation method, and who rotated.
[02:29] Ethan Miles: export options — we push to our S3 bucket and also ingest into Splunk. what's supported?
[02:35] Luis Ortega: we have native export to S3 and GCS, plus a real-time pub/sub stream for SIEM ingestion, and we maintain connectors for Splunk/Datadog. for Splunk we have a HEC-compatible forwarder, for Datadog we can send logs via their intake. you can also stream to a syslog endpoint.
[03:01] Priya Kumar: is the export encrypted with customer-managed keys? we need CMEK.
[03:07] Maya Chen: yes, for Private deployments and dedicated VPC options we support customer-managed KMS in AWS/GCP— you can bring your own key and we encrypt audit logs at rest with that key. for hosted, we offer an option to use a separate encrypted bucket with server-side encryption and we can support CMKs for enterprise contracts— we'll share specifics.
[03:31] Rajesh Patel: retention — what defaults and can we have immutable retention for legal hold?
[03:36] Luis Ortega: defaults vary: hosted default retention is 90 days for audit logs, dedicated customers can configure retention up to 7 years depending on the plan. we also support export to long-term storage automatically to an S3 glacier or GCS coldline if you want immutability, and we can support object lock/immutability depending on customer bucket settings. legal hold is managed by exporting to your bucket with object lock enabled; Redwood won't override your bucket policies.
[04:05] Priya Kumar: ok so workflow would be realtime export to S3 with object lock, and short-term copies for quick console search?
[04:12] Luis Ortega: exactly, we keep an index for 90 days (searchable in Console), and beyond that you rely on your exported copy for compliance retain. you can also configure archiving windows and lifecycle policies.
[04:25] Ethan Miles: about alerts — can we send specific admin events as alerts to our SIEM? e.g., api key revoke or role escalation.
[04:32] Luis Ortega: yes, our event stream supports filtering and rule-based forwarding. we can also publish to a pub/sub topic with selectors so your SIEM only consumes relevant events. There's also a webhook/alerting integration for immediate pushes.
[04:48] Priya Kumar: audit integrity — do you support signed events or checksum so we can prove no tampering?
[04:54] Maya Chen: we provide event hashes in the log payload and you can verify using the exported object. for Private installs you can also enable signed eventing where each event is signed with a key you control. we'll add that detail to the spec we share.
[05:10] Rajesh Patel: what about RBAC change history? do you keep the before/after snapshot?
[05:16] Luis Ortega: yes, we store deltas with before/after where feasible; for big policy blobs we store the reference to the policy version and include a link to the archived policy in the export.
[05:29] [background noise, someone drops a coffee cup briefly]
[05:36] Nadia Thomas: how do you handle cross-account admin actions if we have multiple orgs under one tenancy?
[05:42] Luis Ortega: we tag events with account and org ids; cross-account actions show actor and target account id. you can filter by account in the console and via export queries.
[05:54] Ethan Miles: do you keep a tamper-evident chain for events? like append-only ledger?
[06:00] Luis Ortega: we provide append-only writes to the event store and log sequence numbers; for customers wanting higher assurance we recommend exporting to your immutable storage with object lock, and we can sign events server-side.
[06:16] Priya Kumar: compliance: SOC 2 and ISO, will the exported schema align with our audit firm's expectations?
[06:23] Maya Chen: yes, we've worked with several auditors. the schema includes event_type, actor, timestamp, IP, request_id, before/after, resource ids, and we can provide a mapping doc that shows which controls are covered by which events. we'll share it.
[06:40] Rajesh Patel: what about retention pricing — how much does long-term retention cost for say 7 years of logs?
[06:47] Maya Chen: i'll have pricing details with storage tiers. typically we recommend using your cloud long-term storage (GCS/Glacier) to reduce Redwood costs; we can include transfer automation in the PoC.
[06:58] Ethan Miles: searchability on long-term archives — if we move to Glacier, can we run ad-hoc queries?
[07:04] Luis Ortega: Glacier coldline means longer retrieval times; for ad-hoc queries we recommend exporting to a low-cost searchable index (e.g., Athena on S3 or BigQuery for GCS)— our export can write partitioned JSON/Parquet to make querying cheap.
[07:22] Priya Kumar: SSO tieback — do you include SAML assertion id so we can link with our IdP logs?
[07:28] Luis Ortega: yes we include SAML assertion IDs and OIDC sub claims when available, and timestamp correlation ids.
[07:36] Nadia Thomas: incident response — if there's a suspected compromise, can we get a full activity dump for a user?
[07:42] Maya Chen: yes, we can produce a full audit trail for a user session, including session start, role changes, api key usage, and any deployment actions tied to that user. we can also provide a signed export for chain-of-custody.
[07:58] Rajesh Patel: how long do you keep RBAC logs in the console? you said index 90 days.
[08:04] Luis Ortega: default console index is 90 days for hosted; dedicated/premium can get extended console indexing to 1 year. but again, you should export for long-term retention.
[08:18] Ethan Miles: any limitations on event volume for exports? we plan high-volume activity during peak times.
[08:24] Luis Ortega: export pipeline scales— for heavy customers we recommend dedicated export workers and batching; there is a small buffer during outages but we have guaranteed delivery semantics in Dedicated mode; for hosted there's near-real-time delivery and we can backfill if needed. we'll scope throughput in the PoC.
[08:43] Priya Kumar: legal hold examples — if we need to freeze records after an incident, what's the flow?
[08:49] Luis Ortega: you toggle export to your locked bucket and we pause deletions for events eligible under your retention policy. we don't control your bucket's object lock — you control legal hold via your cloud provider.
[09:02] [screen share of docs referenced: audit-logs-schema.md, export-integration.pdf]
[09:14] Maya Chen: quick note on encryption in transit — everything uses TLS and our service-to-service calls are mTLS within the VPC for Private.
[09:24] Ethan Miles: are logs signed in transit too or only at rest?
[09:28] Luis Ortega: mTLS covers integrity in transit; for event-level signing that's an optional feature as mentioned.
[09:36] Priya Kumar: can you provide a sample SIEM mapping? our SOC wants SPL for Splunk and a JSON mapping for Datadog.
[09:44] Luis Ortega: yes, we'll include Splunk SPL examples and Datadog parsing rules in the packet.
[09:50] Rajesh Patel: any gotchas we should be aware of for VPC/private deploys? network egress for export?
[09:56] Luis Ortega: with Private you control network egress; export to your S3/GCS will happen over internal networking if configured. if you route to external SIEM endpoints you may need allowlists.
[10:09] [brief pause]
[10:16] Maya Chen: quick commercial note — audit logs and basic export are included, long-term retention and CMK support for hosted is part of enterprise add-ons. we'll call that out.
[10:28] Priya Kumar: fine. were there any questions on data residency? we need logs kept in EU for certain subsidiaries.
[10:34] Luis Ortega: we can route exports to region-specific storage; for hosted we have EU regions and can ensure data residency for the exported artifacts. for Private you control where data lives.
[10:46] Nadia Thomas: would you be able to mask or redact certain fields in the export, for example remove user email local-part?
[10:52] Luis Ortega: we provide configurable scrubbing filters on export, you can set field-level redaction rules. it's usually recommended to keep identifiers but we can pseudonymize or hash emails on export.
[11:05] Ethan Miles: what's the SLA around exports? if export delivery fails do you retry?
[11:11] Luis Ortega: yes we have retry/backoff semantics and durable queues. in Dedicated mode we offer stronger SLO-backed delivery; hosted has best-effort with retries and alerts.
[11:23] Priya Kumar: ok, about access control for the logs themselves — who at Redwood can view hosted audit logs?
[11:29] Maya Chen: access is restricted to system processes; human access is rare and audited. we expose logs to customers via Console and exports only; any Redwood support access is via just-in-time access with approval and is itself logged.
[11:45] Rajesh Patel: how is access logged — is support session activity recorded?
[11:49] Luis Ortega: yes, support sessions that access customer data generate audit events including who approved, who viewed, duration, and reason.
[11:57] [crosstalk]
[12:00] Nadia Thomas: what about correlation with infra logs? can you include instance ids or pod ids when relevant?
[12:06] Luis Ortega: we attach runtime identifiers where applicable (node id, container id) for Private/dedicated; for hosted we provide abstracted resource ids.
[12:16] Priya Kumar: any documented breach scenarios where audit logs proved helpful?
[12:21] Maya Chen: we've had customers use the audit trail to identify a compromised service account; the sequence showed api_key.rotate, then an anomalous deployment. auditors appreciated the signed export for chain-of-custody.
[12:35] Ethan Miles: ok, let's get into specifics for PoC: we want a 2-week export for one environment, with Splunk ingestion and retention of 3 years in our bucket. can you support that?
[12:44] Luis Ortega: yes, we'll provision export workers and set up the Splunk HEC endpoint. we'll provide bandwidth estimates for sizing.
[12:52] Priya Kumar: timeline — we need this ready for our auditors by mid-May.
[12:56] Maya Chen: doable, we can aim to have PoC started week of 2026-04-27 and initial exports within 48 hours of setup.
[13:06] Rajesh Patel: can you share the audit-log schema now?
[13:09] Luis Ortega: i'll share right after the call, sanitized examples and mapping.
[13:14] [short silence]
[13:20] Maya Chen: any other blockers?
[13:23] Priya Kumar: none from me. just want to review the schema and the KMS options.
[13:28] Nadia Thomas: please include the signed-event option in writing.
[13:31] Luis Ortega: will do.
[13:34] Maya Chen: cool, i'll recap next steps in the email, send pricing and the schema, and we'll get the PoC scheduled.
[13:42] Priya Kumar: thanks all.
[13:44] Ethan Miles: thanks.
[13:45] [call ends]
